hazards.risk: Gets out of control
hazards.who: Members, other people on site, public
hazards.controls: Should be in designated areas, to avoid embers igniting tents. Fire fighting equipment should be readily available within the area of the campfire.

hazards.risk: Too close; No organisation; No place of safety; No way to fight fire; No clear map of site; Black powder risk
hazards.who: Members, other people on site, public
hazards.controls:
All units should be a minimum of 6 metres apart to prevent the spread of fire
Fire precautions plan
Designated Safe Area
Fire-fighting equipment set up at regular intervals around the campsite
All campsites should have a grid plan, with a copy available for the use of the emergency services.
Black Powder should be stored in accordance with the Black Powder legal requirements

hazards.risk: Flammable liquids
hazards.who: Members, other people on site, public
hazards.controls:
They must be able to show how they are going to store their flammable liquids safely.
Should be apart from the main camping area.
Must have adequate and appropriate fire fighting equipment in their unit.

hazards.who: Members, other people on site, public
hazards.controls: Entrances to campsite are at least 3m wide

hazards.risk: Vehicles can't get on or off; Injury due to poor surface conditions; Emergency services unable to enter or leave site; Gate guard and moving round site; Risk of Injury/loss of life due to loss of control of vehicle; Damage to actual camping area surface; Damage to vehicles plus property
hazards.who: Members, other people on site, public
hazards.controls:
If possible have entrance plus exit, and spare ways out kept unused until end of muster
Restrict movement of traffic to essential services only in adverse weather conditions
Liase with emergency services for the event of an emergency and draw up contingency plans.
Restrict movement of traffic to essential services only in adverse weather conditions
Ensure that no unnecessary personnel are within the entrance area.

hazards.risk: Risk of flood
hazards.who: Members, other people on site, public
hazards.controls: Liase with emergency services for the event of an emergency and draw up contingency plans.

hazards.risk: ground is tinder dry; extreme heat
hazards.who: Members, other people on site, public
hazards.controls:
BBQ ban, fire/smoking restrictions as required
shorter performance times, provide shade for horses, marshall car parks to ensure dogs not left in cars, provide extra water & rehydration salts in medics tent on battlefield.

hazards.risk: Danger of burning to public and reenactors
hazards.controls:
1. Fire fighting equipment must be positioned within the campfire areas.
2. Campfires must always be attended, and safely positioned.
3. Due to the fact a large amount of modern day clothing is highly flammable, the publics safety must always be observed.
4. Because of this the public should have a steward to take them around the site, or stewards should be stationed at high risk areas such as fires, and be responsible for the safety of that area.

hazards.risk: Danger of impaling to public and reenactors
hazards.controls:
5.Sharpened Stakes-Again the fire safety officer was extremely worried about these in an area where the public had access.
6. From a safety aspect these should not have a sharp point, and should be blunted in areas the public have access.
7. Again a steward to maintain safety in this area would be ideal.

hazards.risk: Danger of injury to public; theft
hazards.controls:
8. Equipment- a large amount of working equipment is on view around this site.
9. All precautions must be taken that the public cannot damage either themselves or the equipment.
10. Again any high-risk equipment should have a steward responsible for its safety.
11. Any members of LH holding powder must adhere strictly to safety policy and regulations, and must remain extra vigilant in the care of their musket.
12. Given the fact that the public is in direct contact with members within the Living History site, members taking part have a personal responsibility to ensure their own and the public’s safety.

hazards.risk: Danger of food poisoning or harm to public or re-enactors
hazards.controls:
13. Cooking- there is a high risk of food poisoning if all hygiene, and adequate food preparation is not taken.
14. All meat etc must be from reliable sources and stored and prepared correctly
15. Nothing prepared either within the living history encampment nor at members home in advance of the event is to be sampled by the general public.

hazards.hazard: Explosion/fire caused by direct or indirect heat source
hazards.risk: Premature Ignition; Injury/loss of life.; Damage to Property
hazards.controls:
In the event of a fire on the campsite the powder area is a high-risk area and members must be evacuated for their own safety, and all possible fire precautions taken.
This area must be immediately identified to the fire service on their arrival.
A blast proof/safe area must be maintained at all times around the storage and issue area of powder.
A non-smoking policy must apply in this area.
Hazard signs must be clearly visible that this is a high-risk area.

hazards.risk: Premature Ignition
hazards.controls: Water to be kept at hand to deal with spills at issue.

hazards.hazard: Powder in the possession of non qualified persons
hazards.controls: A set procedure for distribution of powder must be adhered to.

The public should be kept away from this area at all times. Powder can only be issued to members with the appropriate qualifications/licenses.
This area should be secure. (I.e. someone in attendance at all times.)
The Police area firearms officer should be informed of the storage of black powder on the campsite, and is entitled to visit and check that safety plus regulations are being upheld. The fire service should also be informed.
It is the responsibility of the fire master in charge of the powder to ensure all safety regulations are adhered to.
Fire fighting equipment should be readily available in this area.

hazards.risk: Theft of property.; Damage to property-personal and structural.
hazards.controls:
Access to and from the campsite to have camp guard.
If more then one access point gate guard on main entrance, provisions to secure secondary entrances.
If public right of way that has not been closed, members of the public should be escorted across the campsite for their own safety.
Check all persons entering for proof of SK membership.
Have a list, or pre arranged form of identification of non-SK persons who are scheduled to require entry. (e.g. Toilet Cleaning, milkman.)

hazards.hazard: Use of firearms in camping area
hazards.risk: Injury from firearms and ammunition.; Fire started by firearms and ammunition.
hazards.controls: Clear rules state no use of musket/pistol firing on campsite. To be monitored by Commdaning Officers

hazards.hazard: Use of other weapons in camping area
hazards.risk: Injury from other weapons not safely stored e.g. pikes/swords.
hazards.controls: Clear areas for sword and other weapon practice with safety zone. To be monitored by Commanding Officer.

hazards.area: RA9 Pedestrians and Traffic in Camping Areas
hazards.risk: Loss of Life or serious injury; Damage to property by either pedestrians or traffic.
hazards.controls:
Roadways should always be clearly marked.
When possible a one-way system should be used.
Speed limits should be in effect at all times.
Speed limits should be enforced.
Host regiments should have the authority to remove members from the campsite who continually disregard these speed safety limits.
Avoid creating “ blind spots”.
Pedestrians should if possible be kept away from areas that need to have a large amount of traffic movement.
Traffic should be kept away from heavily used areas, such as the beer tent, food vans, powder issue and magazine.
Members should be encouraged not to move their vehicles unless necessary once on site.
Parked vehicles and camping units should not protrude onto roadways.
Medics vehicles should be clearly identifiable and have clear unobstructed access away from the battlefield and site

hazards.risk: Emergency vehicles unable to enter could lead to; (a) Fire being unable to be controlled.; (b) Medical services being unable to reach causalities.; (c) Police unable to reach incidents or assisting the other emergency services.; Health Risk due to cleaning vehicles being unable to gain access to maintain toilet facilities.
hazards.controls:
Members to be informed on arrival either verbally or by leaflet of basic layout of the campsite area.
Restricted areas to be made clear e.g. Magazine has hazard signs.
Host regiment to check roadways are maintained and clear of obstructing vehicles, tents, caravans etc.
Where possible extra parking areas away from the campsite be made available.
Have overflow area available for excess numbers
Where possible have portaloos openings not directly stepping into the roadway. (Recess them a little bit).

hazards.hazard: General overall risk at the inability of members unable to move freely around the campsite
hazards.controls:
Restrict speed limit & have signs.
Campsite entrance designated inwards / outwards traffic lanes.
Where possible have a gate guard person in high viz stationed on the road outside entrance to the campsite to flag down & guide emergency vehicles that have been called (especially where some entrances are blind / narrow angled)
Where possible keep walking public clear of the public entrance gates for vehicular traffic.

hazards.risk: Powder Burns, loss of life, injury and serious injury.; Secondary ignition leading to explosions and fire.; Stabbing, impaling, facial/head injuries., crushing, broken bones; Hearing damage; Smoke inhalation; Slipping/Falling; Damage to personal or structural property.
hazards.controls:
SK medical facilities should be available at all times.
Only members who have been properly trained to SK standards allowed to take part in battles, demonstrations or displays
Commanding Officers and chain of command used to ensure that their members are proficient in their chosen arms.
Measured charges insisted upon, and earplugs recommended
Measured charges insisted upon
Officers to be aware of ground

hazards.risk: Secondary ignition leading to explosions and fire.; Hearing damage; Damage to personal or structural property.
hazards.controls:
Medical facilities for the public must be on hand at all times.
The safety area in front of the public should be regularly checked by the organising regiment to prevent members of the public encroaching onto the battle area. This should be monitored by the Muster Organiser.
Only members and authorised personnel allowed into the safety area – this should be monitored by the Muster Organiser. Persons are authorised by the LGs of each army, Medics, Board of Safety Chair or in an emergency any member of the Board of Directors.
The public should be informed of possible dangers by;
(a) Displayed information.
(b) Information via commentary.
(c) Public to be made aware not to touch anything found on the ground but to inform an SK member ASAP. (
d) Public to be told not to enter onto the battlefield area after the performance however if this is unavoidable then they should be prevented from doing so until it has been thoroughly checked by participating members at the end of each performance after that ‘c’ above applies.
(e) Maximum information to the public to ensure their safety.
All members must be aware of safety issues and be able to advise the public.
Public and SK interaction should be supervised by members familiar with safety issues specific to the circumstances.
Muster planning must include access and egress for emergency vehicles to and from the battle site. Consideration of a suitable area for evacuation by helicopter paying attention to overhead cables, proximity of public, proximity of tentage, the ground clear of debris etc.

hazards.risk: Loss of life.
hazards.controls:
Entrance area should be:
(a) Clearly marked.
(b) Lighted if possible.
(c) Warning signs from approximately 300 yards.
(d) Traffic if possible should not have to cross across on coming traffic.
(e) Members on road entrances should wear reflective safety jackets/coats.
(f) Traffic if possible should not be allowed to queue on the main road when entering the campsite, a reasonable area should be allowed for checking members in.

hazards.risk: Serious injury.
hazards.controls: Police should be informed and any advice, and requirements strictly adhered to.

hazards.hazard: Possibility of entrance area being blocked impeding access for emergency services, and emergency evacuation
hazards.controls: If possible on major events, police should be on duty at busy periods to maintain traffic control.

hazards.risk: Muster organiser is not aware of requirements for Horse
hazards.controls: Master of Horse, CO of Wallers or Rupert's Lifeguard, must inspect site, or send their reprsentative, before the muster, and report that they are satisfied with the provision to the Muster Organiser, in writing.

hazards.hazard: Horse lines within horse lines, mounting and form up area
hazards.risk: Kicks, bites, escape of horse. Harm to cavalry, other re-enactors and public and horses.
hazards.controls:
a) The horses suitability is deemed by the owner, master of horse and senior cavalry officer.
b) Horses must only be corralled within the horse lines
c) The mounting must be the correct size for the horses, taking into consideration, size of and number of horses.
d) Mounting area will not be entered by members of the public.
e) The horses must not be situated in a place that will prevent access for emergency services to the site.
f) Only members of the Sealed Knot, owner grooms may enter the coral or handle the horses
g) Horses must not be left unsupervised at any time.
h) Riders or /and grooms must check the fittings, collars and tethering of horses throughout the day, fixing any lose ropes, or informing the owner /contractor of issues.
i) Water and food levels must be checked throughout the day and add to as necessary.
j) Horses must always have a head collar on when not being ridden.
k) Lead ropes must be easily accessible.
l) There must be a planned rout should the horses need to be moved quickly from the staging / mounting area.
m) Avoid leaving a single horse on the horse lines. If this has to be done the owner/groom must stay with them.

hazards.risk: Falls or kicks; “run offs”; Thrown shoe - land on re-enactor or public; Rider falls
hazards.controls:
a) Riders must be competent and have Sealed Knot accreditation.
b) Riders must be considerate as to the kit they are riding in. They must only complete manoeuvres and displays that are within their ability.
c) Riders must ensure they are aware of any dangers, such as water, pyrotechnics, traffic, street signs in the riding area.
d) The horses welfare must always be considered.
e) Danger to public must be considered during display, the following scenarios must be considered;
f) if in field should be collected at earliest convenience to protect horse, Re-enactors and public.
g) horse welfare to be considered – horse to be contained and captured as soon as possible in a safe a way as possible – assessment of ridder and or owner and officer as to whether they can continue.
h) rider welfare - rider to be checked for injuries. Assessment of rider and or medical team as to whether they can continue.
i) Rider must plan for escape routes
j) Rider must avoid slip and trip hazards for horse
k) Tack failure – owner to ensure all tack is to correct standard, fits horse and is suitable for use. All riders to ensure tack is fitted correctly before riding
l) Dismounted escorts for horses and riders to and from parade. Public should be kept a safe distance for horses in escorts opinion .
m) Should a horse appear to become distressed, they must be removed, with other horses if necessary, and taken back to main horse lines.
n) Organisers should ensure that horses do not have to cross rope on the ground from barriers - rope must either be removed for access, or a proper gate used.
0) If a rider feels unsafe/unwell or not fit to battle, they should make their CO aware and leave the field.

hazards.risk: Artillery and Musket; Pike; Injury or loss of life (human and equine).; Damage to property.
hazards.controls:
a)Riders must be aware of artillery and musket being fired and not engage or ride across loaded pieces. Equine ear plugs can be used if required
b) Pike blocks at point must not be engaged. Pikemen trained not to hit horses with pike
c) All horses used by the Society to be warranted safe by the horse contractor, including shoed and vaccinated
d) Ensure horses cannot be accessed or fed by public or non-cavalry SK members - at least a 3 foot gap, double barrier if possible.
e) Ensure there are enough toilets in cavalry area (at least 3 at minis/majors)
f) Horses in the care of the Society to be ridden in performances or on campsites only by adequately trained and certificated members. (All risks)
g) All training of uncertificated riders to take place away from public areas and campsites.
h) All tack to be checked for safe condition prior to performances and training.
i) All participants to be trained in safe practices regarding use of and contact with horses.
j) Horses not to be ridden at excessive speed in campsites (walking only). or roadways(trotting if visibility of 50m+, or walking)
k) Horses moved through spectator areas to be escorted by members on foot where possible.
l) All riders to wear adequate hard headgear.
m) Provision of adequate safety areas and/or barriers to performance area.
n) Knowledge of the location and availability of local veterinary surgeons
o) Extra RA carried out if there are equine diseases in the area
p) Ensure that all manure is safely disposed of.
Check RA for adverse weather - ground and going.
q) Check RA for adverse weather - ground and going.

hazards.risk: Escape from coral, public entering horse paddock
hazards.controls: a) Horses will not be left unattended on living history when site open to public. Will return to electric fenced paddocks overnight

hazards.risk: Member of public is bitten, stood on
hazards.controls: b) A rope barrier between the horses and public is preferred. Riders must be accompanied by unmounted people and members of the public told not to go behind horses. Riders must be fully aware of surroundings and keep hold of horses.

hazards.risk: Danger of injury to public
hazards.controls: c) Horses to be corraled within living history and not left unattended

hazards.hazard: There is a high risk of collision between vehicles and the marching body from oncoming traffic
hazards.risk: Poor visibility.; Speeding Traffic.; Risks to pedestrians.; Serious injury, loss of life.; Damage to vehicles.; Damage to property.
hazards.controls:
Marshals in High-Viz and/or High-Viz vehicles as escort
Move in orderly fashion without separating the body and in good time
Traffic if possible, should not be allowed to queue on main roads
March to be during daylight hours (unless a specific risk assessment for night marching is carried ou)
Police should be informed and any advice or requirements strictly adhered to.
Route to be planned and checked prior to march proceeding
Marching body should not straddle lane and march with the direction of traffic
Members to be advised of all obstructions overhead and ground level
Public not to handle any weapons
Close supervision of interaction with public
No Firing of Musket (Only in pre-arranged areas with safety area and cornered off)

hazards.risk: Public injury
hazards.controls: Visitors will be separated from the props and only allowed access under supervision.
Musketeers present are trained, fully licenced and NO BLACKPOWDER will be present.
All are trained swordsman; The swords have blunted re-enactor blades. Swordsman to keep own control of sword at all times.
Re-enactors to keep situational awareness, especially of others and ceilings.
Charge boxes will be clean and empty of black powder.
Snap Sack, Food bowl and drinking vessel. Examples of soldier’s rations...which will not be consumed.
Re-entactors to maintain situational awareness at all time
Do not hand weapon fully across to public unless in controlled arena or area where there is no danger to other public. Maintain own grip on artefact/prop as part of this.
Re-enactor to ensure kit is safe and free from sharp edges or burrs
Re-entactors to maintain situational awareness at all time

hazards.hazard: Working with children (under 19s) in school or other situations
hazards.risk: Ensure appropriate Safeguarding procedures are maintained
hazards.controls:
In schools, follow Safeguarding procedures and regulations.
If not DBS cleared, ensure not left unsupervised with any under 19s
Seek full advice from SK Safeguarding Officer and Education Director

hazards.risk: Public injury
hazards.controls: Any swords carried have blunted re-enactor blades. Will not be drawn beyond scabbard. Swordsman to keep own control of sword at all times.
No muskets or powder
Re-enactors to keep situational awareness, especially of others and ceilings. No pikes
Re-entactors to maintain situational awareness at all time
Organisers to ensure that there is no risk of issue with public regarding intoxication, damage or reuptational risk

hazards.risk: Public injury
hazards.controls: Any swords carried have blunted re-enactor blades. Will not be drawn beyond scabbard. Swordsman to keep own control of sword at all times.
No muskets or powder
Re-enactors to keep situational awareness, especially of others and ceilings.
Re-entactors to maintain situational awareness at all time
Organisers to ensure that there is no risk of issue with public regarding intoxication, damage or reuptational risk
Walk the field before the event; mark or fill holes; brief units on known hazards.
Keep battle lines off steep ground; tape off banks; position public on level ground.
Fence or tape off; keep battle and camp clear; brief stewards.

hazards.hazard: Overhead power lines (pikes, colours, tent poles)
hazards.controls: Mark on the site plan; exclusion zone with no pikes or poles raised beneath.
Check for dead branches; keep cavalry clear of low branches; no camping under unsafe trees.

hazards.hazard: Livestock, dung, barbed or electric fencing
hazards.controls: Agree with landowner to remove stock; mark electric fences; clear dung from the battle area.
Mark guy ropes; peg caps; keep walkways clear; lighting at night.
Cylinders upright, outside tents, away from fires; check hoses; no gas in the living history area.

hazards.hazard: Alcohol around fires, weapons and powder
hazards.controls: No drinking before or during battle; no powder handling after drinking; camp rules briefed.
Stop activity in lightning; lower pikes and colours; secure tents and gazebos.
Check the forecast; dry clothing; warm shelter available.
Lost child point; stewards briefed; announcement procedure.
Enough toilets and water points; hand washing near food.
Team lifts; use trolleys; brief on safe lifting.
